unmapped_findings: Critical transformation temperatures of the experimental steel: Ac1 = 705 °C, Ac3 = 950 °C, Bf = 380 °C, Ms = 346 °C (source: b0149).
AN800-T phase composition from EPMA (Table A1, wt%): C 0.02(F)/0.35(B/TM)/0.57(FM)/1.20(RA)/1.20(DIM); Mn 2.70/2.80/3.00/3.80/3.80; Al 2/2/2/1.70/1.70; Si 0.40 in all phases (source: b0154).
After tensile fracture, AN800-T necking region austenite (RA) fraction = 0.004 and P-T-P_AVE = 4.48° (source: figure_012).
AN800-T dimple size statistics: Ave = 1.44 µm, Peak I = 0.59 µm, Peak II = 2.14 µm; fracture surface shows dimples plus some quasi-cleavage facets (source: figure_011, b0131).
At necking strain, B/TM contributed 41% of the flow stress in AN800-T; the maximum stress caused by back stress σ_B = 300 MPa and the GND back-stress contribution = 291 MPa (source: b0128, b0107).
Predicted final deformation-induced martensite (DIM) fraction for AN800-T = 1.16% (Fig. 7(b)); average DIM size c = 0.15 µm (source: figure_007, b0103).

The abstract reports the novel low-density steel with yield strength ≈1 000 MPa and elongation ≈18.7% (source: b0010); the measured AN800-T values are yield strength 985 MPa and elongation 18.7% (source: b0046).
